transcript.answer:
ADR-002 (settled 2026-09-25) decided this after a PR #261 review comment proposed dropping the card and letting the model write free text. Delivery status is always rendered as a deterministic card with `suppressAssistantResponse: true`. The model never phrases a delivery time, ETA or status in prose. The ADR gives these reasons:
1. Hallucination and compliance. The EU AI Act data-flow record and the `docs/danish-review.md` rows promise that the customer reads delivery status verbatim from the TMS. A paraphrased ETA is the one hallucination the pilot cannot afford.
2. Measurability. The card-rate KPI (SC-006, at least 90% by 2026-Q4) counts cards, so a prose answer has no denominator. The thumbs-up KPI (SC-007, at least 80%) also needs the card, because ratings attach to card turns.
3. FR-043 of support-agent-tms-tools. It is being amended specifically to permit a deterministic-render tool, which is the only exception to the ban on `suppressAssistantResponse` and `clientMessages`. Without the card, the amendment has no justification.
4. Not-found case. The not-found card is deterministic too, because the model must not invent a shipment it did not fetch. The ADR calls that a GDPR-adjacent data-integrity risk.
The rejected alternative was the reviewer's concern that a rigid card reduces the model's flexibility.

judgements.reason: The answer covers all gold points: the SC-006 card-rate KPI (at least 90% by 2026-Q4) needing card turns as its denominator, verbatim TMS status as a compliance promise where a paraphrased ETA is the one unaffordable hallucination, and free text proposed on PR #261 and rejected 2026-09-25; the extra details do not contradict the gold answer.
